subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should reset archive recovery be solved as read-only family history only, as a Doctor-owned restore/re-index command, or as both staged surfaces?
rationale: The remaining choice controls whether OpenClaw only exposes archived transcript history for inspection or also mutates session indexes and archived user transcripts, which affects privacy, retention, session identity, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Ship read-only family history first
options.body: Use the bounded `includeFamily`/history-retrieval path as the initial recovery surface and defer mutation or re-indexing until its data model is explicit.

options.title: Add Doctor restore/re-index
options.body: Add a guided `openclaw doctor --fix` style recovery that backs up data, records archive provenance, and makes transcript mutation explicit to users.

options.title: Reject restore mutation
options.body: Keep reset archives read-only through browsing/export APIs and avoid making old `.reset.*` files active sessions again.

recommendation.title: Ship read-only family history first
recommendation.body: Use the bounded `includeFamily`/history-retrieval path as the initial recovery surface and defer mutation or re-indexing until its data model is explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently carried the archive recovery fallback into main and are closest to the remaining history-retrieval boundary.
